fields.meta_description: See what the best startup landing pages do after the click, with 4 worked examples, then build yours from a prompt. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build One of the Best Startup Landing Pages From a Prompt
fields.hero_description: Get a page that does what the best startup landing pages do: one clear promise, one action, every signup in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Each Startup Landing Page Comes With
fields.features_subheading: A visitor sees a headline and a button. Emergent builds what sits behind them, from the database to the domain.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from your description

Tell Emergent what the product does, who buys it, and what a visitor should do next. Emergent builds the page around that, and a new headline or section takes one more prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Signups saved to a database you own

Every email, form answer, and survey vote goes into a table in a database you own. Form responses have no cap. Launch day traffic lands in the same table as your first week.
fields.feature_3:
Your CRM and mailing tool stay in sync

The app sends each new signup to HubSpot, Slack, or any other tool with an API, and pulls data back the same way. The list stays in one place and shows up where you work.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when the right account signs up

Set the rule yourself, such as team size or the plan someone picks. The app emails the founder or posts in Slack when a signup meets it, and sends a reminder a day later.
fields.feature_5:
A live dashboard of what the page is doing

The app shows signups by day, by traffic source, and by headline on a dashboard that updates as visitors arrive. You can read a headline test result on the day it settles.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and code you keep

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, and the page moves wherever the product goes.

fields.tab_content_1:
The problem headline won 31 signups to 17

Saltcrate sells bookkeeping software to food truck owners. Half of its visitors see the problem headline, "Stop doing your books at midnight", and half see a feature headline about receipt scanning. After 800 visitors, 400 per headline, the problem headline had 31 signups and the feature headline had 17.
fields.tab_content_2:
Big warehouse teams go straight to the founder

Talvero makes inventory software. Its form asks how many warehouses a team runs before it asks for an email. Teams with 3 or more get founder Dalia Sundquist's calendar link, and she gets an email. Larkspar Supply runs 5 warehouses and booked a Thursday call with Dalia.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every new clinic adds one to the count on the page

Plinthwise has no famous customers yet, and its page for dental clinics skips the logo strip. A live count from the app's database stands in: 412 dental clinics scheduled shifts this week. When Sorrelby Dental published its first schedule this morning, the count moved from 411 to 412.
fields.tab_content_4:
520 of 1,000 visitors picked the handlebar mount

Before paying for tooling, Lumenvane asked visitors to its bike light page which mount they would buy, and saved each pick with an email. Of 1,000 answers, 520 picked the handlebar mount, 310 the helmet mount, and 170 the seat post. The first production run is handlebar mounts.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Startup Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to build a page like the best startup landing pages: one promise, one action, and a test you can read.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Say who the product is for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose the proof you can show today
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Paste your notes into one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write one line that names the buyer and the problem the product solves for them. That line becomes the headline. If two versions of it compete, keep both and test them in step 6.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide on the single thing a visitor should do, such as booking a call or joining the beta. Give the page one button for it, and cut links that lead anywhere else.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick one piece of proof that is real now, like a live usage count read from the app's database. Leave the logo strip out until the logos are real, and add them as customers agree.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste your notes from steps 1 to 3 into Emergent as one prompt, in plain English. Emergent builds the page and the database table behind its form.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask only for the fields you will use this month. Put the question that decides who gets a founder call before the email field, and drop anything you can ask later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test one change at a time
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run two headlines or two prices against each other and change nothing else. Wait until both versions have the same number of visitors before you read the dashboard.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page. When the product changes, prompt the page to match it, and check that the headline still promises only what ships.

faq_plan.q: What are best startup landing pages?
faq_plan.a: The best startup landing pages are single pages that tell one kind of buyer what the product does for them and ask for one action, such as a signup or a call. They show proof the startup can back up today, and every response lands somewhere the team can use it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create best startup landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Describe the product and the one action you want in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. Emergent builds the page with its form and the database behind it, and you change the headline or add a test by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should a startup landing page say above the fold?
faq_plan.a: It should name the buyer and the problem in the headline, then give one line on how the product solves it and one button. Feature lists and team bios can sit further down the page, where a visitor who wants them will scroll.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in startup landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look at what each page asks the visitor to do and what happens after the click, not only at the layout. A gallery screenshot shows the design, but it leaves out the form and the follow-up behind it. If you sell software by subscription, the saas landing page examples go deeper on plans and trials.

faq_plan.q: Can I build a landing page for my startup without a developer?
faq_plan.hint: How to build a startup landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. You write what the page should say and do in plain English, and Emergent builds it, signup form included. If a developer joins later, paid plans include full code export to your GitHub repository.

faq_plan.q: What proof can a startup show on its landing page before it has customers?
faq_plan.hint: What startup landing page to use?
faq_plan.a: Show what is true today, such as the number of teams in your beta or a pilot user's own words. Ask each pilot user before you quote them by name, and leave out the logos of companies that have not agreed to appear.

faq_plan.q: Should a startup make a separate landing page for each traffic source?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once a source sends enough visitors to read on its own. A page for a podcast mention can repeat the host's offer, and a page for partners can credit the person who sent the visitor. The affiliate landing page guide covers tracked partner links in detail.

faq_plan.q: Which numbers show whether a startup landing page is working?
faq_plan.a: Start with the signup rate, which is signups divided by visitors. Read it for each headline on its own, then for each traffic source. Then check what those signups do a week later. A page that fills the list with people who never come back is not working yet.

faq_plan.q: How often should a startup update its landing page?
faq_plan.a: Update it whenever the product or the buyer changes, and check it against the product at every release. A headline that promises a dropped feature costs trust with each visitor who reads it. In Emergent, a change is one prompt, and the signups stay in the same database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a startup use landing pages for hiring as well as for customers?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A separate page for each open role keeps candidates away from the sales pitch and saves each application to its own table. For role descriptions and application forms, see how recruiting landing pages are set up.

plan.angle: The top 10 for this keyword is screenshot galleries (Dribbble, Landingfolio, One Page Love, Saaspo), a Reddit thread, a Quora thread and two listicles from builders. They show what the best startup pages look like and stop there. This page shows what four of them do once a visitor arrives, each with its rule and its numbers: a headline test, routing big accounts to the founder, a live usage count as proof, and a demand check before a production run. The FAQ covers what makes a page good, what to put above the fold, early proof, measuring it and changing it. SaaS, waitlist, demo and free trial pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build One of the Best Startup Landing Pages From a Prompt", meta title "Best Startup Landing Pages: 4 Examples to Build | Emergent" and hero "Get a page that does what the best startup landing pages do: one clear promise, one action, every signup in a database you own." all carry the primary's whole job (build a startup landing page of that standard), no sibling topic; hero under 130 chars, how-to description one sentence under 140 (QC D1/D2 pass).

intent.evidence: Top 10 is example galleries and listicles; the page delivers 4 worked examples ("Four Startup Landing Page Examples": Headline Test, Founder Calls, Live Proof, Demand Check), a 7-step how-to and a builder comparison, matching the meta promise "4 worked examples". Builder-fit angle carried: "what the best startup pages do after the click".

specificity.evidence: Speaks to founders: "Teams with 3 or more get founder Dalia Sundquist's calendar link", "Leave the logo strip out until the logos are real", "Before paying for tooling, Lumenvane asked visitors"; table generated from the library (V2/V3 pass).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: "Saltcrate sells bookkeeping software to food truck owners.", "Tell Emergent what the product does", "Write one line that names the buyer"; QC Q1 clean.

craft.evidence: Sentences carry one idea each and vary in length: "The first production run is handlebar mounts." No tacked-on endings (Q5 clean). Notes recorded for repeated phrases and the 16 uses of "headline".

voice.evidence: Plain product verbs and unglamorous detail: "Larkspar Supply runs 5 warehouses and booked a Thursday call with Dalia.", "the count moved from 411 to 412". H1 superlative recorded as a note.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to claims_used (database-owned "a database you own", no-caps "Form responses have no cap", custom-domain "included in Emergent and use credits", code-export "On paid plans ... GitHub repository", alerts "sends a reminder a day later"); no third-party facts in prose, so empty domain_sources is consistent; tab numbers add up (400+400=800; 520+310+170=1,000; 411 to 412).

distinct.evidence: Founder-stage stories of its own (proof before customers, demand check before tooling, founder calls); no sibling primary in a heading (K checks pass). Overlap of tab shapes with high-converting-landing-page recorded as a note.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic written questions, none naming a brand or a file format (paa --spec: pass 10, reject 0, flag 0); each answered first ("Yes. You write what the page should say"); hub link in item 2; sibling links saas, affiliate, recruiting; moat lines in items 5 and 9.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches tab copy word for word: Saltcrate 800 visitors, 400 per headline, 31 vs 17; Talvero rule "3 or more warehouses", Larkspar 5, Thursday, "Email to Dalia Sundquist"; Plinthwise 411 to 412, Sorrelby Dental; Lumenvane 520/310/170 of 1,000, "Production run: handlebar mounts". findings.fix: Lead with the outcome, e.g. "Build a Startup Landing Page That Books Founder Calls", if the primary can sit in the title/hero instead.
